posts.title: Chasing the Golden Hour
content: There is a fifteen-minute window after sunrise when the light turns everything to honey. I have been getting up at 5:40 all week to catch it.

Most mornings fail. The fog does not lift, or it lifts too fast, or a truck parks exactly where the light lands. But Tuesday delivered: low sun, long shadows, and a street sweeper kicking up dust that caught the light like snow.
Settings for the curious: 50mm, f/4, ISO 200. The dust did the rest.
comments: That dust shot is unreal. Straight out of camera?

posts.title: Street Frames: One Roll, One Neighborhood
content: The constraint this month: a single roll of Portra 400, shot entirely within four blocks of home.
Thirty-six frames force choices a memory card never will. I passed on shots I would normally take without thinking, and the keepers feel more deliberate for it.
Twelve of the thirty-six came out. That ratio would have depressed me two years ago; now it feels honest.

posts.title: The Fog Series, Continued
content: Part three of an accidental series. The harbor disappears completely about ten mornings a year, and I have decided to be there for all of them.
Fog flattens everything into layers, like a stage set. The trick is finding one dark shape to anchor the frame — a crane, a mast, a person on the pier.
comments: The crane one should be a print. I would buy it.

posts.title: Darkroom Notes: First Prints
content: I finally used the community darkroom membership that has been guilt-tripping me from my wallet since January.
Printing is humbling. The negative I thought was my best of the year printed flat and lifeless; a throwaway frame of the fog series came alive with a little dodging.
Next session I want to try split-grade printing. Notes to self included below so future me has no excuses.

posts.title: Why the 50mm Never Leaves the Camera
content: Every few months I try to love another lens, and every few months I come back to the nifty fifty.
It is not the sharpness, though it is sharp. It is that the frame matches how I see before I raise the camera. No zooming with feet, no wide-angle drama. Just the scene, cropped by habit.

drafts.title: Notes on Shooting in the Rain
content: Half the shots this week were made under an umbrella held in the wrong hand. A few of them are keepers, and the rest are lessons about lens hoods.
Try the pier at blue hour before the lamps come on. Bring the tripod this time.

drafts.title: Film vs Digital, Again
content: I promised myself I would stop writing this post. Here we are. The short version: film for the walks, digital for the work.

drafts.title: Printing Big: A 24x36 Experiment
content: The lab said the negative would hold up at that size. The lab was mostly right, and the grain is now a feature.
